angle: Bottom up. I listed every exit destination, transition end and staying sentence of family A's 29 unplaced dynamics (71 items, counted from the entries; 2 dynamics have no items) and grouped those that state the same condition in different theorem wording. Read in full: each entry in dynamics.json (mechanism, exits, transitions, compose, forbids, beyond, open), places-v1.json, the decisions' wording, pilot-hanging.json, the first two sections of WHOLE-PICTURE.md. Lean statements checked for the sentences the grouping turns on: RegimeMargin.ends_iff_below, holds, stays_ended, ends_beyond_giving, not_before, falls_within, rises_superadditive, Adjusted.falls_iff_below, Coupled drains and the Chain.cascades witness, Web.continuing_restores, Web.late_return_finds_none. The chapter sections and the rendered family page I did not read through; the assignments rest on the atlas wording plus those statements. Clusters that recurred (number of items touching each): a level that holds because taking is met by giving (about 21); taking above what comes back, the level still standing (10, plus one item the pilot left hanging); below a need or cut off, return not excluded (12); below a point from which it falls to nothing, or a state that cannot be had again (existing past-turning-back, 15); no longer going on (existing ended, 14); still going after the thing it depended on was lost (7); going on only while another does (3 items, though four mechanisms state it); a state that can be had again (6). Nine items state no condition at all but a law of every edge or a kind of arrow. Names were given last.

new_places.gloss: What is taken from a stock is no more than what comes back to it, so its level holds and those who depend on it go on. No rule or judge need be involved.
new_places.example: Such as a woodlot cut each winter by no more than it grows in a year.
new_places.test: The law says a level, a floor or a membership is HELD under a standing taking: the level never falls below its start, a floor is kept at the next step, everything is active and supplied at every step, a present member is present after the step. Also an item that is a threshold, a sign or a pace inside that holding (for example fluctuations slowing as the edge nears). If the law's conclusion is that the level falls, it is not this place.
new_places.needed_by: About 21 of 71 items: 10 stay in or lie inside it (margin-of-a-regime transition 1 'from H + y up the level never falls below its start'; ending-laws-as-regimes-on-a-lineage exits 1, 2, 4; consumption-ends-with-feeders exits 2, 3; slowing-down-before-an-own-end transition 1), and 11 arrows start or end in it (the restoring witnesses Restored.returns and Bridged.bridged; a-rule-with-no-holder transition 2 'a constant take at most the renewal: the level does not fall').
new_places.also_in_families: H (most of it: restraint-within-the-joint-slack, never-leaving-a-guard, renewing-consuming-formation, becoming-renewal-reading, horizon and step couplings kept); B as the place its drains start from (horizon-optima-hold-the-greatest-renewal, keeping-forgoes-the-renewal-at-the-need); G (unceasing-generation-needs-renewal); F (closed-cycle-without-dissipation, lossless-exchange).

new_places.gloss: More is taken from a stock than comes back, so it falls step by step, though it still stands above what its dependents need. How long this lasts is set by what is left.
new_places.example: Such as a household that spends more each month than it earns, out of savings.
new_places.test: The law's premise is that over a stretch taking exceeds what is given back (uptake above replenishment for n steps, a draw beyond all giving, taking from something given nothing, takers multiplying on a fixed stock, a constant take of the renewal plus d), the level not yet at nothing, and the law bounds how long that lasts or says what follows. No rule or judge appears in the statement; where the statement is about a rule that does not register the taking, the item belongs to the existing 'uncounted'.
new_places.needed_by: 10 items, and one the pilot could not place: ending-laws-as-regimes-on-a-lineage transitions 1 to 3 (n steps of excess from a stock below n + m; doubling takers last at most log2(level + 1) generations; a lineage reproduces at most the starting stock many steps); consumption-ends-with-feeders transition 1 and exits 1, 4; margin-of-a-regime transitions 3, 4; pilot-hanging persisting-filters-what-was-chosen exit 1 becomes an arrow from here to ended.
new_places.also_in_families: B (nearly every entry: own-count-misses-joint-excess, drawers-in-turn, re-optimizing-above-a-renewal-ends-it, where-a-rising-take-ends, whole-drawing-beyond-renewal-ends); H (renewing-consuming-formation, becoming-renewal-reading); G (closing-needs-net-draw). The pilot's readers asked for it by this description.

new_places.gloss: What something needs is not arriving, or stands below its need. It goes on only by what it has stored, if anything. Whether it is still there when supply comes back depends on the store and the wait.
new_places.example: Such as a seed in dry ground waiting for rain, or a town through a siege.
new_places.test: The law is about a stretch in which something's supply is absent or below its need (unsupported, unfed, under a cut, a level at or below a need) and the law does NOT say it cannot return: it says how long the thing lasts and on what, or whether returning supply finds it. If the law says nothing can bring the level back (a gate, a fixed draw below the point), the item is past-turning-back; if the subject is the stock still above the need and falling, past-renewal.
new_places.needed_by: 12 items: reserve-defers-ending transition 1 and dormancy-over-a-stretch transition 1 and exit 1 (a reserve of at most n lasts at most n unsupported steps; support returning within the reserve finds it); a-reader-rebuilt-from-its-stock transition 1 (under a cut, present after k + 1 steps from a level of at least 2(k + 1)); market-finite-support-obstruction's three items; exit-from-a-margin transition 1; three-outcomes-of-a-loss exits 1 and 3.
new_places.also_in_families: E (a-circular-wait-needs-a-reserve-present, thresholds-of-waiting, a-pair-tolerates-only-within-a-window); H (the-stock-buys-time-where-the-rebuild-draws-on-it, recoverable-mediated-change, supported-renewal-recovery, two-sided-regulation-and-late-reading); B (others-drawing-first-end-the-base).

new_places.gloss: What it depended on is gone and has not come back, yet it goes on: it needs that thing less, has moved to another, or never needed it. The new source may be drawn down in turn.
new_places.example: Such as a fleet that sails to the next fishing ground when one is fished out.
new_places.test: The law says something is still going after a thing it depended on was lost without return, and that its dependence on that thing has weakened, dissolved or moved to another; or that what goes on never depended on what ended. The law need not say whether the taking has stopped: an item that says the taking continues after the move, or stops with it, lies inside this place.
new_places.needed_by: 7 items: three-outcomes-of-a-loss exit 2 (still active after a loss without return means the dependence weakened or dissolved) and exit 3's second run; consumption-ends-with-feeders exit 4 and substitution-preserves-consumption exits 1, 2 (stays active by switching, still consuming, the one that sustained it ends); confined-rise-within-a-whole exit 1; ending-laws exit 3.
new_places.also_in_families: H (succession-on-a-funded-carrier, formed-goal-revision-continuation, a-regularity-kept-and-changed); B (what-a-rise-draws-from-beyond, position-does-not-protect); G (where-the-possible-grows).

new_places.gloss: It goes on only while something else does, or only while every one of several does. If that one ends, so does it, at once or once what it has stored is used.
new_places.example: Such as a roof on three rafters, or a parasite with a single host.
new_places.test: The law says one thing goes on ONLY WHILE another does, or only while each of several does (it gives nothing wherever nothing is left of the other; a whole active exactly while every part is; every later member depending on one stock; two that each end alone and hold together), and says what follows for it when the other ends or holds. The mirror of the existing 'holds itself in place': there what holds it is its own results, here something else.
new_places.needed_by: 3 items, and the main laws of four mechanisms that list no item for it: a-whole-of-every-part exit 1 (AllWhole.persists_iff: active exactly where every part is); a-cascade-along-total-dependence exit 1 (the cascade stops at a link not drawn on); confined-rise-within-a-whole exit 1. The cascade law itself (Coupled.Indexed drains, the end of one ends everything downstream), co-ending-along-dependence, the confined rise and 'groups on one family end together' state this place in their mechanisms but have no exit or transition for it.
new_places.also_in_families: B (others-drawing-first-end-the-base, whole-drawing-beyond-renewal-ends, position-does-not-protect, no-finite-part-bears-taking); H (mutual-dependence-and-its-pace, whole-persists-through-generation); E (a-circular-wait-needs-a-reserve-present, as 'waiting on each other' if that family makes it mutual).

new_places.gloss: Where it has been can be reached again from wherever it goes next: it goes round, or no step it takes closes the way back.
new_places.example: Such as a field rotated through three crops, back each fourth year to where it began.
new_places.test: The law says a state can be had again from wherever its steps lead (it returns, it is kept, it lies on a cycle), or that every path enters such states, or it concerns the one step at which this stops being so (a fork with one step after which it can still be had and one after which it cannot). Staying in one state for good is the limiting case and may be split off by the family of rest; a law about a level held under a taking is within-renewal, not this.
new_places.needed_by: 6 items: every-loss-passes-a-juncture exits 1, 2 and transition 1 (keeping only the steps after which s can still be had keeps s; every loss passes a fork); basins-of-a-determined-law transition 1 (within m listed states every path enters what returns before step m); necessarily-drawn-is-not-returning exit 1; a-cascade-along-total-dependence exit 3 (a pair that moves between two states for ever).
new_places.also_in_families: F (its recurrence entries and cycles; F may also need a separate 'swinging, nothing held yet'); G (rest as the limiting case; returning-novelty-forgetting-on-levels); H (a-regularity-kept-and-changed).

what_the_layer_shows:
Family A is not a region of endings. Placed, it is one line of level with three ways off it. The line: living within what renews it, living past it, short of what it needs, past turning back, ended. Off 'short' and 'past turning back' go the three outcomes that one law (three-outcomes-of-a-loss) names: supplied again (back to within-renewal; seven items, five of them witnesses), living on something else now, or ended. That law says the three are constrained, not exhaustive or exclusive, and its witness has all three follow one break. Of the 71 items, 31 are arrows between two places, 14 stay, 15 lie inside a place (11 of them say where the edge of past-turning-back lies and how it moves), 3 lead out, 8 are unresolved; one further item is a single witness with three arrows.

Where it joins the existing 15. (1) past-turning-back and ended are shared outright: the pilot's 'too late' and A's 'below the point' are one place, and family B's reading-a-loss-in-time exit 3 already runs from the pilot region to margin-of-a-regime. (2) past-renewal sits beside uncounted: the same falling stock, without and with a rule that scores the outcome alike. The pilot's hanging item persisting-filters exit 1 becomes past-renewal to ended. (3) held-by-another mirrors holds-itself: held up by something else against held up by its own results. A's own texts say the two can hold at once ('attraction is not continuation': a hold can go on while what it stands on is drawn down), which is the pilot's judged-inside seen from the stock's side; no item of A proves that join. (4) Drift joins several-ways, all-on-one and fixed-rule with two items and a compose. (5) The fork law would join felt if felt's test is widened.

Conspicuously not joined. (a) Nothing in A leads INTO within-renewal except restoring: how anything comes to live within what renews it is not here (family H's ground; 'how parts first come to live as one' is listed open). (b) within-renewal to past-renewal has only parameter arrows (the draw grows, the take rises by d); what makes a taking grow is family B's. (c) past-renewal to past-turning-back rests on a fixed draw or the gate; without the gate the only items are witnesses of return. (d) Nothing leaves ended or past-turning-back inside the same law. The only exits are 'another rule of the family' (taught or rebuilt from outside), which the entries themselves say is not a path out; drawn truthfully these are stubs pointing off the map. (e) The two halves of A are joined by no item: the root laws about states that can or cannot be had again (can-return, the fork) and the stock laws about levels (the line above) share only past-turning-back as a destination. 'Return grades renewal' is family F's entry and has no items. (f) held-by-another to ended is stated by four mechanisms (the cascade along total dependence, co-ending, the confined rise, groups on one family ending together) but only one exact item carries it (AllWhole.persists_iff); co-ending-along-dependence and degeneration-from-a-horizon have no items at all, so two proved laws put nothing on the map. (g) Nine items are not places: five are one law of every edge proved three times (leaving a kept region takes a step that does not keep it; a line out has a step going out; a change of something kept passes a gated step), and four are a reading that sorts arrows into kinds, none proved. Both belong in the legend. (h) The two market entries join the line only roughly, in the model's own numbers.
layout: A circuit with two ways off it, not a ladder. Put within-renewal left of centre with can-return directly beside it on the outer left (the two 'comes back' places: a state had again, a level made up again). From within-renewal draw the line rightward through past-renewal and short, level with each other, so left to right reads as how much is in hand, not as better to worse. The restoring arrows curve back over the top from short and past-renewal to within-renewal, closing the circuit; this is where most of the witnesses are and it should look like a loop, since a thing can go round it many times. From short, one way off continues right to past-turning-back and on to ended (both already on the pilot's map: keep them where they are and bring A's line to meet them, so the pilot's chain and A's line converge on the same two nodes from different sides). The other way off rises from between short and past-turning-back to elsewhere, set above and to the right, with open space beyond it toward family H: it is a continuation, and nothing in A says where it goes next. held-by-another sits below the line under past-turning-back and ended, with its arrow rising into ended, and across the page from holds-itself so the pair can be seen as a pair. past-renewal should sit directly under or over the pilot's uncounted, close enough to read as the same stretch with and without a rule. The fork arrow from can-return to past-turning-back runs along the bottom, under the stock line, joined to it only at its far end: that visible separation is finding (e). The two stubs out of ended ('another rule, brought in from outside') point off the page edge. Legend, not nodes: the edge law and the four kinds of arrow.
doubts:
1. Three neighbours may be one too many. Under a fixed draw, 'below the point' is past-renewal, short and past-turning-back at once; I sorted by what the law concludes (how long the excess lasts; whether return is excluded; that it falls to nothing). A second reader may merge past-renewal and short. What would be lost: past-renewal is about a stock still above the need with something still coming back, short about a dependent whose supply is below its need, and their exits differ (a feeder against a store).
2. held-by-another has only 3 items. I propose it because four mechanisms state it and B, E and H will need it, but by the rule 'no place that no item needs' it is the weakest. Without it those three items go to ended and elsewhere with their origin unnamed.
3. can-return overlaps what F (cycles, swinging) and G (rest) will propose. A needs it as the origin of the fork arrow and for the root entries; F should own the wording.
4. 'Made good again' is not proposed. In A restoring is an arrow back to within-renewal (seven items), not a condition anything stays in. If another family makes it a place, A's restoring arrows could pass through it.
5. Nine items (the edge law five times over, the four routes) are left unresolved on purpose as legend. The two attraction exits could instead be drawn as the only way out of past-turning-back.
6. Thresholds: I put the edge laws inside past-turning-back, following the pilot's decision on loss-read-in-time transition 3, and drew one side of each iff as an arrow to ended and the other as staying in within-renewal. A later reader may prefer each exact threshold as one both-sided mark between the two places.
7. Rough assignments I would not defend: a-rule-with-no-holder transition 1 (the from-place is really 'a rule kept up by members teaching members', likely H's); market-model transition 1 (existence of a low region, not entry); the compose (a join, not a change); consumption transition 1 and reserve transition 1 as arrows to ended although the laws give a step of inactivity, finality being a separate premise in dormancy-over-a-stretch; threshold-in-the-state-plane, where 'rests below the draw' is not shown to be level nothing.
8. ended is asked to take 'absent and not made from within' (no holder, an empty pool, a share of none). If that reads as a stretch, a separate place 'not there, and nothing here makes it' is the alternative; A alone has only two items for it, both stubs.
9. Reading limits: I read every entry in full and the Lean statements named under 'angle', but not the chapter sections or the rendered family page, and I ran nothing. Item numbers follow decisions.json (counted from 1). The Chinese labels are mine by ear and unreviewed; 入不敷出 is the common idiom for past-renewal and 吃老本 for short, if an alias is wanted.
